descriptions: in every body, 'in the breath of the breath'
the one of Hindu and Turk
the Beloved whose redness colours the lover
known in sahaj, beyond the three qualities
negations: not in temple, mosque, Kaaba or Kailāsa
relation_to_self: The Lord dwells within the self as musk in the deer; when the 'I' goes, Hari is; like gold and bracelet, water and wave (Ravidās).
relation_to_world: The world is māyā's play and Kāl's grinding-mill, yet the Lord pervades it; Hindu and Turk, caste and sect are human constructions.
caveat: The Sants would reject any reading that makes their Rām an avatāra or an image, or that reduces their Beloved to an impersonal abstraction; they also resist being enrolled in any scriptural system, Hindu or Muslim.

descriptions: the True Being of Satlok, beyond the three worlds
incarnate as Kabīr in every age
negations: not Kāl Nirañjan, the creator of the three worlds
relation_to_self: The soul (haṃs) is of the Sat Puruṣ's substance, fallen under Kāl, and returns to Satlok by the true Name.
relation_to_world: The three worlds are Kāl's creation and prison; Satlok alone is true.
caveat: The Kabīr Panth's cosmogony and its worship of Kabīr as God sit uneasily with the Bījak's apophatic critique; the Kabīr Chaurā and Pārakh readings stress discernment over mythology.

names.name: Rām / the one known by pārakh

descriptions: what remains when every doctrine has been tested as the mind's creation
negations: no name that can be written
relation_to_self: The discerning self is not deceived by the gods and doctrines the mind makes.
relation_to_world: The world of doctrines is the mind's; delusion (bhram) is to be dissolved.
caveat: The Pārakh reading (Pūran Sāhib) borders on declining to posit any ultimate beyond discernment itself; recorded as a low-confidence characterization.

descriptions: Lord of Satlok who sent Kabīr and established Dharamdās's line
relation_to_self: The soul is freed by the Name received from the vaṃś ācārya.
relation_to_world: The three worlds are Kāl's.
caveat: As for the Kabīr Panth generally; the hereditary line is itself part of the soteriology.

names.name: Alakh / Allāh (as the one Lord of Hindu and Turk)

descriptions: the stainless one saluted first in the Vāṇī
met in the unseen
Brahman one without a second (Sundardās)
relation_to_self: The Lord is within the body, which is the true mosque and temple; the self erased, Hari remains.
relation_to_world: One Lord of all beings; hence no enmity toward any.
caveat: Sundardās's Advaita and Dādū's devotional voice coexist; the panth would reject a reading that erases devotion to the guru and the Name.

descriptions: sandalwood to the devotee's water
the Lord of the poor who raises the lowly
the king of Begampura
negations: no difference between you and me in truth
relation_to_self: As gold and bracelet, water and wave.
relation_to_world: Begampura: a world without grief, tax, fear or rank is the Lord's city.
caveat: The modern Ravidassia Dharam distinguishes itself from Sikh readings of the same hymns; recorded as context.

descriptions: the stainless formless one
relation_to_self: Realized within by yoga and devotion.
relation_to_world: The world is his play.
caveat: Low-confidence characterization from the sect's name and Rajasthani context.

descriptions: the nirguṇa Rām loved by his 'lovers'
relation_to_self: Remembered within.
relation_to_world: Pervades all.
caveat: Low-confidence characterization.

descriptions: both the nirguṇa and Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa
relation_to_self: The guru is above Hari (Sahajobāī).
relation_to_world: Created by Hari; transcended through the guru.
caveat: The sampradāya holds nirguṇa and saguṇa together; it would reject a purely impersonal reading.

descriptions: the true name of the formless Lord
relation_to_self: The true name within.
relation_to_world: All castes equal before him.
caveat: Three distinct movements; characterization low confidence.

descriptions: Lord of Satlok who appeared as Kabīr
negations: above the gods of the three worlds
relation_to_self: Freed by his Name.
relation_to_world: The three worlds are lower creation.
caveat: Low-confidence characterization.

descriptions: the ocean of consciousness and love from which the sound current flows
reached beyond Sach Khand
negations: beyond Brahm, the god of the Vedas
relation_to_self: The soul (surat) is a drop of that ocean; it returns and merges while retaining (on most accounts) the bliss of love.
relation_to_world: The lower creation is Kāl's domain; the Supreme's mercy (Dayāl) acts through the Saints.
caveat: Sant Mat ranks other traditions' ultimates (Brahm, Nirañjan, Pārbrahm) as lower regions — a hierarchy that those traditions do not accept.

descriptions: the true name revealed by Soamiji
relation_to_self: The surat is its drop.
relation_to_world: As in Sant Mat.
caveat: The Agra lines hold that the name itself was newly revealed by Soamiji; other Sant Mat lines treat it differently.

descriptions: the Lord of love, source of the Shabd
relation_to_self: As in Sant Mat.
relation_to_world: As in Sant Mat.
caveat: As in Sant Mat.

descriptions: the Word heard as sound and seen as light, in all scriptures
relation_to_self: The soul is of the same essence.
relation_to_world: The Word creates and sustains all.
caveat: Presented as the common core of all religions — a claim the religions named do not themselves make.

descriptions: reached through light and sound to the soundless
relation_to_self: The self realizes itself in the soundless.
relation_to_world: All scriptures point to it.
caveat: Low-confidence characterization.

names.name: the Man of the Heart (maner mānuṣ)

descriptions: dwells in this human body
near yet a hundred thousand leagues away
seen through the guru
worship of the human makes one golden
relation_to_self: The Man lives in one's own body, neighbour in the mirror-city, unseen until the guru reveals him.
relation_to_world: What is in the body is in the universe; the world outside is known through the body.
caveat: The Bāuls refuse the scriptural names and doctrinal frames (Vedāntic, Vaiṣṇava or Islamic) in which the 'one truth' might be stated; the ultimate is the living human, verifiable in the body.

descriptions: the truth of man, above which there is nothing
the union of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa within the human pair
negations: not known by the one who has not crossed the darkness
relation_to_self: Every person's true form (svarūpa) is Kṛṣṇa or Rādhā.
relation_to_world: The eternal Vṛndāvana is within the body.
caveat: Orthodox Gauḍīyas reject the identification of human partners with Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; the Sahajiyā rejects the orthodox reading as merely outward.

descriptions: the one Master present in the living guru
hidden in the human form
negations: not the many gods of outward custom
relation_to_self: The Kartā is found in the human, above all the guru.
relation_to_world: Outward custom is kept for the world's sake; the truth is secret.
caveat: The tradition's double life means its outward Hindu observances should not be read as its view of the ultimate.

descriptions: the founder as God
relation_to_self: Devotion to the founder.
relation_to_world: Caste religion rejected.
caveat: Low-confidence characterization from ethnographic reports.

descriptions: merciful to the poor
relation_to_self: Found in the human.
relation_to_world: Hindu and Muslim equal.
caveat: Low-confidence characterization from ethnographic reports.
